reason: Both conversations correctly identified E17 as a fill/supply fault, got the customer to open the half-closed isolation valve, confirmed the fix with a rinse cycle and correctly recommended no part. Conversation 1 did it with two focused questions and a short, well-targeted reply that prioritised the valve check and deferred the filter, matching the homeowner's stated reluctance. Conversation 2 reached the same result but opened with a long dump covering six causes, a bucket test and pliers-based filter removal (asserting the filter is 'the most common cause' and 'in most cases' the fix, which was unsupported here), though it did include the proper turn-off/unplug boundary and a sensible post-fix drip check. Conversation 1's efficiency and better-paced questioning edge it ahead; Conversation 1's reference to 'hot and cold' taps on a cold-fill-only model is a minor slip.
